source.title: Deep Learning in current Neuroimaging: a multivariate approach with power and type I error control but arguable generalization ability
source.authors: C. Jim'enez-Mesa; J. Ramírez; J. Suckling; J. Vöglein; Johannes Levin; J. Górriz; A. Adni; D. I. D. (dian)

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly permutes training labels and measures performance. Its results and conclusion say the tested models generally did not fit corrupted data with accuracy similar to the original data, qualifying the broad random-label claim.
record.gate_note: The paper permutes labels in three neuroimaging datasets and reports accuracy for permuted and original data. The results test random-label fitting, but do not test the other listed versions. The paper's claims about fitting corrupted labels in its Introduction cite prior work and are not treated as its own results.
record.test_reason: The study measures random-label classification by linear SVMs on autoencoder features, rather than random-label fitting by supervised deep networks trained with stochastic gradients. The autoencoders minimize input reconstruction MSE; randomized class labels train the SVM, with additional one-component PLS reduction for resubstitution. These results therefore do not test the specified versions. The authors' capacity interpretation does not establish a counterexample to V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion that their implemented models generally fit corrupted labels less accurately than original labels, and that CV training and test errors can diverge. Their prediction that more sophisticated architectures will increase fitting capacity is an interpretation, not a demonstrated result. Their conclusions concern AE–SVM pipelines and validation methods.
record.recipe_differences: Uses autoencoders for feature extraction with a linear SVM classifier, label permutations, and CV or upper-bounded resubstitution; it does not reproduce the original studies' standard deep-network random-label experiments. The authors state hyperparameters were maintained across original and permuted data.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and task design; validation method (CV, resubstitution, upper-bounded resubstitution); feature extraction within versus outside the permutation loop.

fits_no_version.finding: Across Tables 2–8, AE–SVM pipelines achieve random-label CV training accuracies of 0.4066–0.7175 and approximately chance held-out accuracy. Raw resubstitution accuracies are 0.3375–0.6187; these use an additional one-component PLS representation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear classifiers on reconstruction-trained autoencoder representations show limited fitting of randomized labels in these neuroimaging settings.

fits_no_version.finding: RUB subtracts a theoretical bound from raw resubstitution accuracy. Near-chance corrected scores do not mean the fitted classifier itself has near-chance training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bound-corrected resubstitution provides conservative performance estimates for the tested linear classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.5 and Tables 9–10 also report randomized-label performance with feature extraction outside the permutation loop. Raw resubstitution accuracy is near nominal chance, while several CV training accuracies remain elevated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixing extracted representations before label permutation changes random-label classification performance and variability in AE–SVM pipelines.

record.problems: The experiments use AE-SVM with a linear classifier and low-dimensional PLS features, rather than testing a range of standard deep networks. Datasets are small. Results vary by dataset and validation method; some uncorrected resubstitution training accuracies on permuted labels are above chance. Training time and convergence rates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out; 28 rows cover reported permuted-label accuracy entries relevant to V1 in Tables 2–8. Original-label scores are recorded as baselines rather than separate rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard supervised deep networks trained with stochastic gradients, including near-zero training error and chance test error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time multiplier relative to true labels and convergence changes across corruption fractions. CV-versus-RUB computational costs do not measure these.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A corruption-fraction sweep showing perfect training fit and progressively worsening test performance.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing them.
Training trajectories establishing that shared real-data patterns are learned before label noise.

record.verdict_notes: All supplied numeric entries match Tables 2–8. The decisive scope issue is that Adam optimizes reconstruction MSE, rather than randomized classification labels. The record also overlooks Tables 9–10 despite saying no rows were omitted; those results likewise fit no listed version. No verdict follows from chance held-out accuracy alone or from subtracting a theoretical bound from training accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: The models are AE-SVM systems, not the standard deep networks and stochastic-gradient training setups in the claim; the paper does not test completely random labeling across conventional architectures or establish test error at chance for all settings.
Training-time multiplier and convergence speed across corruption fractions are not measured.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
The paper tests full label permutation, not a sweep from no corruption to complete corruption.
The paper does not compare weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
The paper does not track whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

relation.reason: The introduction and conclusion discuss neural-network capacity to fit corrupted labels, but the reported AE–SVM experiments do not directly test the catalog's claim versions.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure classification by linear SVMs using reconstruction-trained autoencoder features, with one PLS component for resubstitution. They do not test random-label fitting by the supervised deep networks specified in V1 or another claim version.

source_check.notes: R20 follows Table 6's correction of 0.1358; section 4.2.2 inconsistently states 0.0960. Upper-bounded resubstitution accuracies are corrected estimates, not observed training accuracies.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: ADNI AD-HC and corrected resubstitution results across datasets
reader_labels.reason: Permuted-label accuracy is near chance under upper-bounded resubstitution in ADNI, MCI binary and multiclass, and DIAN (R4, R12, R16, R24); CV training accuracy is also near chance or substantially below true-label results in ADNI and MCI (R1, R9, R13). This challenges the claim for these tested AE-SVM settings.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Uncorrected resubstitution and DIAN/HC CV training results
reader_labels.reason: Some permuted-label training or resubstitution accuracies remain above chance, including the MCI HC and DIAN HC subsets; the evidence does not support a universal inability to fit any signal in the permuted labels (R7, R15, R17, R19, R21, R23, R25, R27).
